statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band because CME equity index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress holds in the high band on a 5.18% ten-year yield, WTI at $92.41 with the Strait of Hormuz closed, Trump's rejection of Iran's seven-day reopening roadmap, Tehran's refusal to soften its conditions, and an IRGC underwater-drone seizure claim that CENTCOM denies.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise behind part of Friday's oil decline would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures still shut, while Iran's refusal to soften its Hormuz terms, a denied IRGC drone-seizure claim and a 5.18% ten-year hold Stress high into the 22:00Z restart
body: Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path at this assessment time and the low current Tail reading reflects an absent path rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 129.23 points or 0.42% from a 30,478.90 prior close and inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 within a 14.68-15.94 range. The latest H.15 release, dated 25 September for 24 September values, shows the two-year at 4.87%, the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47%, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%, so equities are absorbing a bond market near multi-decade yield highs. Weekend evidence hardened further rather than easing. Trump rejected Iran's phased proposal on record, and Foreign Minister Araghchi has since said Tehran is awaiting a definitive response through mediators while refusing to soften the conditions attached to a seven-day reopening: lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions, releasing frozen funds and observing a regional ceasefire. Araghchi also said Iran is ready for a doomsday war while keeping indirect talks open. The IRGC Navy claimed it seized a second U.S. Remus 600 underwater vehicle in the strait, which CENTCOM publicly denied, stating positive control of all operational drone assets; Iranian army commander Hatami separately said the war is not over and reiterated the closure. Houthi launches toward Saudi Arabia on 26 September were intercepted, with two drones reported en route to Riyadh and ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait. The material market consequence is that part of Friday's 2.33% WTI decline to $92.41, and the parallel 2.14% Brent decline to $104.32, rested on a diplomatic premise that has now been explicitly withdrawn, and neither oil nor equity futures have traded since. That creates a genuine but narrow reopening-gap and two-way-discovery mechanism at the 22:00Z restart rather than evidence of a formed one-way path, which is why the danger window is confined to the restart and early Asian hours instead of being widened across the session. Shared Finviz context was read and is both stale at roughly 115 minutes and partial, with its calendar and futures sections unavailable; its usable latest-session breadth from Friday showed Technology up 0.85%, six of eight megacaps higher with wide dispersion between MSFT at +3.66% and META at -3.33%, and six of seven tracked semiconductors higher. That tone is delayed, non-real-time context with no source as-of and cannot establish current NQ structure, so it informs Stress and Confidence only. Stress is raised to the high band on the yield backdrop, the unresolved strait closure, the withdrawn diplomacy and a catalyst stack that runs through Wednesday's core PCE and Micron results, Thursday's ISM and Friday's payrolls into quarter-end rebalancing. Confidence is high because current index, volatility, yield, oil and calendar levels were verified directly from primary sources, but it is held below the very-high band by the single unavoidable gap: no live price path exists until the futures restart.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were carried forward unchanged without hindsight revision. Tail held in a narrow 6-9 band, Stress rose steadily from 53 to 72, and Confidence decayed from 78 to a 67 trough around 08:00Z before recovering to 79 by 18:00Z and easing to 77. The mapped state remained EA_ON with dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a closed-futures weekend in which risk accumulated through headlines rather than through an observed price path.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours, so the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline for the remainder of Sunday, then peaks inside the published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where Iran's refusal to soften its Hormuz terms, the denied IRGC drone-seizure claim and Friday's now-unsupported oil decline meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. From the early Asian hours the path steps back down on the assumption that reopening imbalance is absorbed with visible retracements, then rises again modestly into Monday's 13:30Z U.S. cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed print, which are checkpoints rather than structural Tail drivers, and once more into the 19:00Z power hour on quarter-end rebalancing. Every elevated forecast hour is conditional gap or continuation risk; none asserts that one-way structure has already been observed. Stress stays high throughout on a 5.18% ten-year yield and an unresolved strait closure, and Wednesday's core PCE, Micron results and quarter-end, Thursday's ISM and Friday's payrolls dominate the wider week.
